To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ascorbateglutathione cycle is the major defence mechanism against oxidative stress in plants, and that the activity of the enzymes in the cycle can be manipulated by molecular genetic techniques to confer increased tolerance to stress.

the ascorbate glutathione cycle is an important antioxidant defence system that protects plants against oxidative stress, that the activities of individual enzymes in this pathway are important in determining the level of protection against oxidative stress, and that the activities of enzymes of this pathway are regulated by a variety of mechanisms.

the antioxidative defence mechanisms in transgenic tobacco plants expressing increased levels of the chloroplast-localised enzymes ascorbate peroxidase and/or glutathione reductase are capable of providing a degree of protection against oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which plants protect themselves against stress, and with the manipulation of the stress response to produce more tolerant plants.
the study of plant metabolism in relation to the production and removal of reactive oxygen species and the role of antioxidants in protection of the plant against oxidative damage.
the mechanisms of plant responses to stress and the application of genetic engineering to the improvement of crop plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidative defence enzymes are important in protecting plants from stress.

(i) the antioxidative defence mechanism of plants is complex and highly regulated, (ii) the enzymes involved are important in protecting plants against oxidative stress, (iii) the enzymes are important for normal metabolism, and (iv) it is possible to manipulate the activities of these enzymes by genetic engineering and to achieve a degree of tolerance to stress.
transgenic plants are proving to be a valuable tool to investigate the role of antioxidant enzymes in plant defence systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transgenic plants have provided a powerful tool with which to study the mechanisms involved in the protection of cells from stress.
transgenic plants have been used to study the role and regulation of the antioxidant defence system in plants.
the ascorbate and glutathione pools and the enzymes of their metabolism are essential components of the antioxidative defense system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antioxidative defence enzymes can protect the plant cell against stress.

transgenic plants can provide a powerful tool to understand the complex interplay between different enzymes and metabolites, and to manipulate the levels and activities of individual enzymes to improve stress tolerance.
it is possible, in principle, to engineer stress tolerant plants through the manipulation of antioxidant enzymes.
